questions.stem: How many leading bits do 10110100 and 10110011 have in common?
questions.explain: Compare from the left: 1,0,1,1,0 match, and the sixth bits (1 and 0) differ. So 5 leading bits agree.

questions.stem: A router splits 120 Mbps of traffic equally across 4 equal-cost paths. How many Mbps does each path carry?
questions.explain: Equal shares mean 120 / 4 = 30 Mbps per path.

questions.stem: Which layer forwards packets between different networks using IP addresses?
questions.explain: Routers work at the network layer. The data link layer moves frames within one network, and the transport layer runs only at the end hosts.

questions.stem: A 1000-bit packet crosses 3 links in a row. Each link runs at 1 Mbps (10⁶ bits per second) and the router waits for the whole packet before forwarding it. How many milliseconds does the transmission take in total, ignoring propagation?
questions.explain: Each link takes 1000 / 10⁶ s = 1 ms to send the packet. Store-and-forward repeats this on every link, so the total is 3 ms.

questions.stem: A graph has edges A–B with weight 2, B–C with weight 3 and A–C with weight 7. What is the cost of the cheapest path from A to C?
questions.explain: The direct edge costs 7, but going A to B to C costs 2 + 3 = 5, which is cheaper.

questions.stem: An undirected graph has 5 edges. What is the sum of the degrees of all its vertices?
questions.explain: Every edge adds 1 to the degree of each of its two ends, so the degrees add up to 2 × 5 = 10.
